item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
In this figure, PQ and RS are parallel.

[Image: Parallel lines PQ and RS intersected by a transversal]

Of the following, which pair of angles has the sum of 180°?
item.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrowheads at both ends are intersected by a transversal line that slopes upward from lower-left to upper-right. The upper horizontal line has label P at its left end and Q at its right end. The lower horizontal line has label R at its left end and S at its right end. At the intersection with line PQ, four angles are numbered: angle 1 in the upper-left, angle 2 in the upper-right, angle 3 in the lower-right, and angle 4 in the lower-left. At the intersection with line RS, four angles are numbered: angle 5 in the upper-left, angle 6 in the upper-right, angle 7 in the lower-right, and angle 8 in the lower-left.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In the figure, PQ and RS are intersecting straight lines.

[Image: Intersecting lines PQ and RS]

What is the value of x + y ?
reference_items.figure_description: Two straight lines intersect. Line PQ slopes downward from upper-left (point P) to lower-right (point Q). Line RS slopes upward from lower-left (point R) to upper-right (point S). At the intersection, an angle arc indicates the obtuse top angle between ray P and ray S, labeled 150°. An arc indicates the acute angle on the left between ray P and ray R, labeled x°. An arc indicates the acute angle on the right between ray S and ray Q, labeled y°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

What is the value of x + y?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines are shown: line l on top and line m on the bottom. Points A and D lie on line l, with D to the right of A. Points B and C lie on line m, with C to the right of B. Line segments AB and AC connect the two lines, forming triangle ABC. A dashed arc indicates that angle DAC measures 55°. reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

- Row 1: A triangle (3 sides).
- Row 2: A four-sided polygon (quadrilateral) with a dashed line segment connecting two opposite vertices, dividing the polygon into 2 triangles.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three right-angled triangles labeled Figure 1, Figure 2, and Figure 3 from left to right:
- Figure 1: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left corner, a horizontal base, and a vertical left side. A vertical line segment connects the hypotenuse to the base near the acute right-most vertex.
- Figure 2: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-right corner, a horizontal base, and a vertical right side. A vertical line segment connects the hypotenuse to the base near the acute left-most vertex.
- Figure 3: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left corner, a shorter horizontal base, and a longer vertical left side. A horizontal line segment connects the vertical left side to the hypotenuse near the acute top vertex.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

[Image: Overlapping triangles ABC and DEF]

What is the measure of angle EGC ?
reference_items.figure_description: Two overlapping triangles, ABC and DEF, resting on a shared horizontal baseline containing points B, E, C, and F in that order from left to right. Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. Side AC intersects side DE at point G. Angle B is labeled 40°, and angle F is labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
